meta.title: Tool Research Ledger
meta.currentBatchNote: Public candidate normalized to an inspectable E0 evidence ceiling; private and internal trial artifacts are excluded.
meta.scope: A 71-option public source-review ledger. The application is reproducibly tested, while third-party tool claims remain E0 until public-safe proof is included.
meta.privacy: The catalog excludes private documents, customer data, credentials, raw OCR text, transaction rows, and source page images.

reports.label: Evidence model
reports.kind: Evidence promotion contract and proof boundaries

reports.label: Research methodology
reports.kind: Catalog review, validation, and decision method

meta.publicEvidenceBoundary: All catalog entries are E0 in this release. Internal reports, private inputs, runtime trials, and static-scan artifacts are not part of the public evidence graph.

assuranceModel.notice: Source review, static scan, runtime trial, and adoption scope are independent. A scan is not a runtime test; installation is not proof of benefit.

grading.observedGradeNotice: A numeric score is shown only when a tool was locally executed and its output was adjudicated. Public documentation review remains E0 and receives no invented score.

decisionScale.IMPLEMENT: Implement a bounded method or control now
decisionScale.CONDITIONAL: Use only within the named scope and controls
decisionScale.REFERENCE: Mine patterns; do not install wholesale
decisionScale.WATCH: Track until a defined trigger justifies testing
decisionScale.HOLD: Do not use until prerequisites and authorization exist
decisionScale.REJECT: Not suitable for this project now

findingScale.NEEDS_VALIDATION: Documented by the repository; not locally reproduced
findingScale.REJECTED: Claim or option rejected for the current scope

intakeGate: Record source URL, reviewed date, license, deployment shape, and data path
Statically inspect skills, scripts, dependencies, and network behavior before install
Pin a commit or version and run only in an isolated, synthetic-data smoke test
Preserve row-level or finding-level evidence for correctness claims
Require independent review for critical, financial, or security conclusions
Promote scope only after a representative corpus and explicit failure outcomes

evidenceLevels.label: Source review
evidenceLevels.description: Official repository documentation and license reviewed; no local execution.

evidenceLevels.label: Smoke test
evidenceLevels.description: Tool runs on synthetic or non-sensitive input; correctness is not adjudicated.

evidenceLevels.label: Controlled benchmark
evidenceLevels.description: Real input with source-adjudicated results and preserved findings.

evidenceLevels.label: Representative corpus
evidenceLevels.description: Labeled cases span target variation and known failure modes.

evidenceLevels.label: Independent validation
evidenceLevels.description: A separate reviewer or production-like process confirms results.

evidenceLevels.label: Monitored production
evidenceLevels.description: Sustained results, drift controls, incidents, and rollback evidence.

capabilityGroups.label: Document intelligence
capabilityGroups.purpose: Recover, inspect, and prepare PDFs or scanned records
capabilityGroups.lead: OCRmyPDF for searchable PDFs; PaddleOCR for extraction research
capabilityGroups.useWhen: A document workflow needs source-adjudicated extraction or controlled PDF preparation.

capabilityGroups.label: Audit and financial controls
capabilityGroups.purpose: Preserve evidence, reconcile outputs, and require human sign-off
capabilityGroups.lead: Existing evidence gates plus selected Financial Services patterns
capabilityGroups.useWhen: A conclusion affects money, compliance, or an external auditor.

capabilityGroups.label: Design and interface quality
capabilityGroups.purpose: Raise visual quality without adding overlapping design stacks
capabilityGroups.lead: Existing design-system and visual-QA gates; local design skills remain conditional
capabilityGroups.useWhen: A dashboard, site, or product UI needs design direction, QA, or animation.

capabilityGroups.label: Skill governance
capabilityGroups.purpose: Screen, compare, and selectively adopt agent instructions
capabilityGroups.lead: SkillSpector as intake gate; libraries as references only
capabilityGroups.useWhen: A new skill or agent instruction bundle is proposed.

capabilityGroups.label: Repository intelligence
capabilityGroups.purpose: Understand codebases and preserve traceable findings
capabilityGroups.lead: Graphify pilot for local code-only maps
capabilityGroups.useWhen: A large unfamiliar repository makes reading and navigation expensive.

capabilityGroups.label: Development control
capabilityGroups.purpose: Specify work, isolate changes, and keep execution bounded
capabilityGroups.lead: Spec Kit method + existing execution gates
capabilityGroups.useWhen: A build needs explicit requirements, acceptance tests, and clean lanes.

capabilityGroups.label: Files, data, and media
capabilityGroups.purpose: Automate structured files and manage local media without hiding data or rights boundaries
capabilityGroups.lead: Use the smallest specialist tool that matches the file, service, or authorized media workflow
capabilityGroups.useWhen: A repeatable spreadsheet, conversion, transfer, Workspace, or personal-media task exists.

capabilityGroups.label: Agent platforms
capabilityGroups.purpose: Evaluate high-agency runtimes and browser control planes separately from the working environment
capabilityGroups.lead: PinchTab is the next bounded browser candidate; no platform replacement is recommended
capabilityGroups.useWhen: Only after a missing capability, isolation model, budget, and rollback plan are documented.

capabilityGroups.label: Knowledge and research
capabilityGroups.purpose: Organize sources, compare models, and support cited synthesis
capabilityGroups.lead: LLM Wiki synthetic/public pilot; DevDocs for offline reference
capabilityGroups.useWhen: Source volume or offline reference needs exceed ordinary search.

capabilityGroups.label: Model engineering education
capabilityGroups.purpose: Learn transformer internals and training systems
capabilityGroups.useWhen: The project goal is education or low-level model experimentation, not production tooling.

capabilityGroups.label: Career operations
capabilityGroups.purpose: Structure job evaluation and application materials with human control
capabilityGroups.useWhen: A separate, privacy-controlled career project needs repeatable triage and drafting.

capabilityGroups.label: AI usage economics
capabilityGroups.purpose: Measure local agent token and cost patterns
capabilityGroups.useWhen: Agent spend or configuration overhead needs evidence before optimization.

Keeping role-specific research agents, memory, approvals, and run history in one local workspace
Testing engine fallback and durable agent workflows without committing to one model provider
weaknesses: The desktop, server, Docker-computer, and installer paths are explicitly experimental
It overlaps substantially with the current Codex workflow and adds a backend, database, agent runtime, credential store, and operational upkeep
It is single-owner rather than a multi-user organization workspace, and connectors and mature team delegation remain limited
The pinned frontend production tree has unresolved critical and high advisories, and its source-checkout UI did not build on this Windows pilot host
risks: The pinned frontend production dependency tree reports one critical and two high vulnerable packages; adoption is blocked until it is updated and rescanned
Host tool execution can run as the signed-in user; Docker computers are optional and experimental rather than a universal safety boundary
The system stores conversations, memory, credentials, schedules, approvals, and run history, creating a sensitive local control plane
Unsigned installers, early development, limited clean-machine verification, and no automatic update path increase maintenance and supply-chain burden
Routines run only while the backend is available, do not automatically retry failed or interrupted runs, and webhook deliveries are not de-duplicated
Single-owner authentication and paired devices are not suitable for an untrusted multi-user deployment
tools.implementation: Keep on HOLD and do not connect private repositories or install globally. First update Next.js to a non-vulnerable release, prove an offline-reproducible Windows UI build, correct or gate the Windows path/ACP/symlink failures, and repeat the identical intake with a scoped real engine. Preserve cost, latency, output adjudication, approvals, cleanup, and a comparison with the current Codex workflow before considering E2.
reentryTriggers: Repository intake or evidence maintenance becomes repetitive enough to justify a persistent local agent workspace
A disposable machine or isolated user profile is available for the pilot
The current Codex workflow can be compared against one identical timed research task
Credential, network, storage, backup, and deletion controls have named owners

tools.summary: A research framework that recursively proposes, probes, and composes changes to the prompts, guardrails, memory, tools, skills, scripts, plugins, and orchestration around an agent.
bestFor: Comparing agent-harness variants on benchmark tasks
Research on prompt, tool, memory, and orchestration improvements
weaknesses: Official benchmark runs target Linux rather than this Windows file-based dashboard
Setup requires Python, uv, Node, cloud credentials, and benchmark-specific dependencies
Its research benchmarks do not directly measure this dashboard's newcomer usability
risks: The documented Codex executor runs with its sandbox disabled and unrestricted network access
Model-backed runs require credentials and can create material token and cloud cost
Recursive optimization can overfit one task unless the evaluation set and acceptance rules are fixed
Benchmark setup clones dependencies and downloads task data
tools.implementation: Use the Propose, Probe, Compose structure manually for this project. Do not install or run Harness² on this Windows workspace. Reconsider only in an isolated Linux environment with synthetic tasks, budget caps, network restrictions, scoped credentials, a pinned revision, and an independent holdout evaluation.
reentryTriggers: A repeated agent workflow has a measurable benchmark and enough volume to justify harness optimization
An isolated Linux runner with scoped credentials and cost controls is available
A holdout set can test generalization beyond the task used for recursive refinement

Multi-width visual linting and before/after review
weaknesses: Large overlapping instruction and script surface
Browser and image workflows add dependencies and network behavior
A strong house method can conflict with an existing product system
risks: Static analysis is critical and incomplete, including process, network, external-action, and SSRF-pattern findings

First adjudicate the script-level findings and unresolved references; only then run a project-local synthetic page trial with hooks, image generation, remote photos, and network access disabled, followed by independent browser QA and rollback.
reentryTriggers: A synthetic trial can isolate its value from existing design skills
